skill.name: stack-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze project stack and recommend skills. Auto-detects frameworks, activates generic ai-dev-kit skills, and optionally scaffolds project-specific skills in the target repo.
skill.summary: Recommend development skills from a detected technology stack and optionally scaffold project-specific guidance.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: All 46 static alerts were dismissed after contextual review, including manual inspection of the three templates. One semantic finding identifies unsafe scaffolding writes that can overwrite files outside the intended destination. No evidence found of credential theft, data exfiltration, or audit-manipulation instructions.

remediation.issue: Scaffolding writes to relative files without entering the generated skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve every output beneath the approved destination, reject existing files and symlinks, and use unique temporary files before atomic replacement.

remediation.issue: The scaffolding example uses an unquoted target path and inserts the project name directly into a sed expression.
remediation.suggestion: Validate project identifiers, quote target paths, enforce repository containment, and use literal template replacement instead of interpolating sed syntax.

remediation.issue: Template names contain unquoted placeholders, and the generation example prepends a comment before YAML frontmatter.
remediation.suggestion: Quote placeholder names, render them before loading, keep frontmatter first, and validate each generated skill before activation.

semantic_findings.title: Scaffolding Writes Are Not Confined to the Destination
semantic_findings.description: After copying the template, the example uses '> temp && mv temp SKILL.md' without changing directories. Following it can overwrite the caller's SKILL.md; a preexisting temp symlink can redirect truncation to another writable file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete scaffolding block contains relative writes and no destination directory change or collision checks. Damage requires executing the documented example with scaffolding enabled.

content.user_title: Match Your Project Stack to Development Skills
content.value_statement: Choosing relevant AI development skills requires understanding project dependencies and conventions. This skill maps detected technologies to recommendations and provides optional project-specific scaffolding guidance.
actual_capabilities: Delegates technology detection to the library-detection skill and organizes its results into a stack report.
Matches file patterns and dependencies to configured skill recommendations, including BAML, Supabase, ORM, Tree-sitter, MCP, FastAPI, and React guidance.
Identifies research, domain, and testing scaffold candidates from project structure and configured thresholds.
Provides three starter skill templates for research workflows, domain vocabulary, and custom testing patterns.
Documents separate report, activation, and scaffolding options for ai-dev-kit integration.
Defines a generated-file manifest and uninstall notice for tracking persistent project artifacts.
limitations: Requires external ai-dev-kit skills and commands that are not included in this package.
Templates contain project placeholders and unfinished sections that require customization and frontmatter validation.
The scaffolding shell example needs destination safeguards before execution because relative writes can overwrite files.
The configuration references an API template that is absent, and the illustrated cookbook and reference files are not bundled.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Repository
use_cases.description: Generate a stack summary and explain which generic skills match the detected dependencies before making changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Setup
use_cases.description: Review proposed activations and project templates while keeping generated artifacts separate from plugin-owned files.

use_cases.title: Document Custom Testing Conventions
use_cases.description: Use the testing template as a starting point for project fixtures, naming rules, coverage targets, and cleanup requirements.
use_cases.target_user: QA engineers maintaining specialized test suites

prompt_templates.title: Summarize My Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository with stack-analyzer. Report detected technologies and recommended skills without activating anything or creating files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain a report without project changes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Each Recommendation
prompt_templates.prompt: Match detected dependencies to configured skill rules. Explain the evidence and priority for each recommendation, and identify unavailable dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review why each skill is relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Project-Specific Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify research, domain, and testing scaffold candidates. Show detection evidence, proposed destinations, and required customization without creating files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: assess template suitability before scaffolding.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold With Explicit Approval
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose scaffolds and request approval. After approval, validate destination containment, refuse overwrites, render placeholders, validate frontmatter, and update the manifest.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: create reviewed project guidance with explicit file protections.

best_practices: Start with a report-only review and verify the detection evidence behind each recommendation.
Approve scaffolding destinations explicitly, reject overwrites, and validate rendered templates before activation.
Keep generated artifacts in the manifest and review them separately when removing the plugin.
anti_patterns: Activate every recommendation without checking whether its detection evidence applies to the project.
Execute the scaffolding shell example unchanged in a directory containing important files.
Treat unfinished templates or missing companion skills as complete, installed functionality.

faq.question: Does this package detect frameworks independently?
faq.answer: No. Its workflow delegates detection to the external library-detection skill and then matches the results against recommendation rules.

faq.question: Does analysis modify my repository by default?
faq.answer: The documented defaults disable automatic activation and scaffolding. Report generation is enabled.

faq.question: Which project templates are included?
faq.answer: Research, domain, and testing skill templates are included. The configured API template is not present.

faq.question: Can I execute the scaffolding example unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Add destination containment, overwrite protection, and safe temporary-file handling before execution.

faq.question: Are generated templates ready for immediate activation?
faq.answer: No. Replace project placeholders, complete unfinished sections, and validate the frontmatter before loading them.

faq.question: What happens to generated skills after plugin removal?
faq.answer: Project-specific skills remain in the target repository. The manifest tracks generated artifacts so users can review and remove them separately.
